newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid to take Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid to take Q4 charge.

text.p: Polaroid Corp said it will take a charge of $15 million to $20 million in the fourth quarter as part of a sales, marketing and development deal with Sterling Diagnostic Imaging Inc.
The charge will cover adjustments to inventory values, fixed assets, employee severance programs and other costs associated with the Sterling agreement, Polaroid said.

Sterling has acquired Polaroid's assets relating to the hardware manufacturing, worldwide marketing, sales and servicing of the Helios Laser Imaging sytems. No figures on the transaction were released.

The two companies entered into a long-term agreement under which Sterling and Polaroid will develop new technologies and products for the medical diagnostic imaging marketplace, the first of which will enter the market in 1997.
Polaroid will supply Sterling with dry, digital film manufactured at its New Bedford, Mass. plant and will also acquire a 15 percent stake in its parent, SDI Holding Corp, based in Glasgow, Delaware.

"We believe that Sterling Diagnostic imaging will accelerate Helios' sales in the diagnostic imaging marketplace worldwide through Sterling's extensive distribution network," said Gary DiCamillo, chairman and chief executive officer of Polaroid.
The agreement is expected to close by the end of November, Polaroid said.
